hello.note: Said with palms pressed together, at any time of day. More formal: नमस्कार (namaskaar).

goodbye.note: Literally 'we'll meet again'. नमस्ते (namaste) is also said when leaving.

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness comes from the -nuhos verb ending (often said -nus) and a soft न (na).

thank_you.note: Nepalis thank less often than English speakers; the English 'thank you' is also widely used.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'it's nothing' — Nepali has no set reply to thanks.

yes.note: Literally 'it is'. Politer: हजुर (hajur). Often you answer by repeating the question's verb.

no.note: Literally 'it isn't'. For 'there isn't / I don't have', say छैन (chhaina).

sorry.note: For small slips the English 'sorry' is also very common.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'please listen'. You can also call out दाइ (daai, 'brother') or दिदी (didi, 'sister').

good_morning.note: Formal or written; in person most people simply say नमस्ते (namaste).

how_are_you.note: Also very common: सन्चै हुनुहुन्छ? (sanchai hunuhunchha?), 'are you well?'

im_fine.note: To ask back: अनि तपाईंलाई? (ani tapaainlaai?)

my_name_is.note: The verb हो (ho, 'is') comes at the end, after the name.

where_from.note: Also asked: तपाईंको घर कहाँ हो? (tapaainko ghar kahaan ho?), 'where is your home?'

im_from.note: A woman says: म …बाट आएकी हुँ (ma …baata aaeki hun).

speak_english.note: Also natural: तपाईंलाई अङ्ग्रेजी आउँछ? (tapaainlaai angreji aaunchha?)

dont_understand.note: Literally 'I didn't understand' — Nepalis use the past tense here.

speak_slowly.note: न (na) at the end softens a request, like adding 'please'.

what.note: If you didn't catch something, हजुर? (hajur?) is the polite 'pardon?'.

how_much.note: Also common: यो कति हो? (yo kati ho?)

where_bathroom.note: In everyday speech ट्वाइलेट (twaailet) is just as common.

what_time.note: The answer uses the same verb: तीन बज्यो (tin bajyo), 'it's three o'clock'.

what_means.note: Casual: यो भनेको के हो? (yo bhaneko ke ho?)

six.note: Devanagari digit: ६. Sounds the same as छ (chha), 'is'.

tea.note: Usually milky and sweet; black tea is कालो चिया (kaalo chiyaa).

bread.note: Means flatbread; sliced loaf bread is पाउरोटी (paauroti).

im_hungry.note: Thirsty: मलाई तिर्खा लाग्यो (malaai tirkhaa laagyo).

bill_please.note: Also common: हिसाब गरिदिनुहोस् (hisaab garidinuhos), 'please settle the account'.

enjoy_meal.note: Nepali has no fixed 'bon appétit'; hosts say this ('eat heartily').

straight_ahead.note: To a driver: सिधै जानुहोस् (sidhai jaanuhos), 'go straight on'.

stop_here.note: 'Right here' is यहीँ (yahin). Drivers are often called दाइ (daai, 'brother').

airport.note: In everyday speech most people say एयरपोर्ट (eyarport).

hotel.note: Also means a simple restaurant; a cheap place to stay is often a लज (laj).

train_station.note: Nepal has few trains; the bus station is बसपार्क (baspaark).

want_to_go.note: No word for 'to' is needed: मलाई पोखरा जानु छ (malaai pokharaa jaanu chha).

one_ticket.note: When counting things, 'one' is एउटा (eutaa), not एक (ek).

cheaper.note: To bargain: अलि घटाउनुहोस् न (ali ghataaunuhos na), 'lower it a bit'.

pay_card.note: मिल्छ? (milchha?), 'is it possible?', works for asking permission for almost anything.

closed.note: Also the word for a general strike, when shops stay shut.

good_evening.note: Formal or written; in person most people simply say नमस्ते (namaste).

good_night.note: Among friends the English 'good night' is very common.

wait_moment.note: Casual: एक छिन है (ek chhin hai), 'just a sec'.

call_police.note: The official word is प्रहरी (prahari). Police emergency number in Nepal: 100.

im_lost.note: Also: मैले बाटो बिराएँ (maile baato biraaen), 'I've lost my way'.

pharmacy.note: People also say मेडिकल (medikal) or फार्मेसी (faarmesi).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: मेरो फोन चोरी भयो (mero fon chori bhayo).

be_careful.note: Gentler, when someone leaves: सम्हालेर जानुहोस् (samhaalera jaanuhos), 'go carefully'.

no_problem.note: Casual: केही छैन (kehi chhaina) or ठिक छ (thik chha).

maybe.note: As a one-word reply, होला (holaa) is very common.

im_tired.note: Also: मलाई थकाइ लाग्यो (malaai thakaai laagyo).

welcome.note: At the door hosts usually say आउनुहोस्, आउनुहोस्! (aaunuhos, aaunuhos!), 'come in'.

my_family.note: In everyday speech also घरका मान्छे (gharkaa maanchhe), 'the folks at home'.

mother.note: Many city children say मम्मी (mammi). Also a respectful way to address an older woman.

father.note: Also बा (baa) or बाबा (baabaa); in cities many say ड्याडी (dyaadi). Formal: पिता (pitaa).

brother.note: An older brother; a younger brother is भाइ (bhaai). Brothers: दाजुभाइ (daajubhaai).

sister.note: An older sister; a younger sister is बहिनी (bahini). Sisters: दिदीबहिनी (didibahini).

child.note: 'Sons and daughters', the usual word for one's children. Son: छोरा (chhoraa), daughter: छोरी (chhori).

friend.note: Same word for a woman. A close friend is मिल्ने साथी (milne saathi).

this_is_my_friend.note: Same for a female friend. More respectful: उहाँ मेरो साथी हुनुहुन्छ (uhaan mero saathi hunuhunchha).

are_you_married.note: A common, friendly question in Nepal. Formal: तपाईं विवाहित हुनुहुन्छ? (tapaain bibaahit hunuhunchha?)

have_children.note: To ask how many: कति जना छन्? (kati janaa chhan?)

monday.note: Every day name ends in -बार (baar), 'day of the week'.

saturday.note: Nepal's weekly day off; most offices and schools are closed.

weekend.note: Mostly written. People say शनिबार (shanibaar), Nepal's day off, or विकेन्ड (wikend).

what_day.note: For the date: आज कति गते? (aaja kati gate?) — Nepal uses its own calendar, Bikram Sambat.

hundred.note: Devanagari digits: १००. सय (saya) on its own also means 'a hundred'.

thousand.note: Devanagari digits: १०००. 100,000 is एक लाख (ek laakh).

how_old.note: Also: तपाईं कति वर्षको हुनुभयो? (tapaain kati barshako hunubhayo?)

years_old.note: A woman says: म … वर्षकी भएँ (ma … barshaki bhaen).

red.note: Like most adjectives in -o, it becomes -aa with plural nouns: राता फूल (raataa phul), 'red flowers'.

this_one.note: Also just यो (yo), 'this'. वाला (waalaa) works like the English 'one'.

that_one.note: For something far off: ऊ त्यो (u tyo), 'that one over there'.

another_one.note: अर्को (arko) can also mean 'a different one'; 'one more' is also अझै एउटा (ajhai eutaa).

its_hot.note: Feeling hot yourself: मलाई गर्मी भयो (malaai garmi bhayo).

its_cold.note: For cold things like water, use चिसो (chiso): पानी चिसो छ (paani chiso chha).

its_raining.note: Literally 'water is falling'. Also: पानी पर्दै छ (paani pardai chha).

beautiful_day.note: Literally 'how nice the weather is today!' — the natural way to say it.

summer.note: In summer: गर्मीमा (garmimaa). The monsoon that follows is बर्खा (barkhaa).

winter.note: Same word as for cold weather. In winter: जाडोमा (jaadomaa).

have_reservation.note: A woman says: मैले कोठा बुक गरेकी छु (maile kothaa buk gareki chhu). Also: मेरो बुकिङ छ (mero buking chha).

room.note: Any room, at home too. Hotel staff also say रुम (rum).

passport.note: The official word, printed on it, is राहदानी (raahadaani).

luggage.note: Also means 'things' in general. A bag is झोला (jholaa) or ब्याग (byaag).

check_out_time.note: Without English: कति बजेसम्म कोठा छोड्नुपर्छ? (kati bajesamma kothaa chhodnuparchha?)

bus.note: A shared minivan is a माइक्रो (maaikro). Any vehicle, bus included, is often just गाडी (gaadi).

next_train.note: Nepal has few trains; for buses: अर्को बस कति बजे छ? (arko bas kati baje chha?)

is_this_seat_free.note: Also: यहाँ कोही बस्नुहुन्छ? (yahaan kohi basnuhunchha?), 'is anyone sitting here?'

i_work_in.note: मा (maa), 'in', joins the word: म बैंकमा काम गर्छु (ma bainkmaa kaam garchhu).

im_student.note: Same for a woman. Also: म पढ्दै छु (ma padhdai chhu), 'I'm studying'.

office.note: On signs and for government offices: कार्यालय (kaaryaalaya).

meeting.note: In offices people often say मिटिङ (miting).

im_busy.note: Also very common: मलाई फुर्सद छैन (malaai phursad chhaina), 'I've no free time'.

day_off.note: Often just बिदा (bidaa): भोलि मेरो बिदा हो (bholi mero bidaa ho), 'I'm off tomorrow'.

colleague.note: Same for a woman. In speech often अफिसको साथी (afisko saathi), 'office friend'.

lets_start.note: Often with ल (la), 'right then': ल, सुरु गरौँ (la, suru garaun).

good_job.note: Mostly to juniors or kids. To anyone: धेरै राम्रो गर्नुभयो! (dherai raamro garnubhayo!)

table_for_two.note: जना (janaa) counts people: तीन जना (tin janaa), 'three people'.

what_recommend.note: Literally 'what's tasty here?'. Also: के खाँदा राम्रो होला? (ke khaandaa raamro holaa?)

not_spicy.note: A little spicy: अलिकति पिरो (alikati piro). Chilli is खुर्सानी (khursaani).

vegetarian_food.note: On menus and in speech also भेज (bhej), as in भेज मोमो (bhej momo).

more_water.note: थप्नु (thapnu) means 'top up'; it works for rice and dal refills too.

no_sugar.note: Ordering it: चिनी नहालेको चिया (chini nahaaleko chiyaa), 'tea without sugar'.

im_full.note: To refuse more food, say पुग्यो, पुग्यो! (pugyo, pugyo!), 'that's enough!'

takeaway.note: To ask first: प्याक गर्न मिल्छ? (pyaak garna milchha?)

it_was_delicious.note: भयो (bhayo), 'turned out', is the usual past here; थियो (thiyo), 'was', also works.

keep_change.note: Casual: भइगो, राख्नुहोस् (bhaigo, raakhnuhos), 'that's fine, keep it'.

head_hurts.note: Works for any body part: पेट दुख्यो (pet dukhyo), 'my stomach hurts'.

need_rest.note: Also: मलाई आराम गर्नुपर्छ (malaai aaraam garnuparchha), 'I have to rest'.

feel_better.note: Without अलि (ali), 'a bit', it means you've fully recovered.

get_well.note: Also: चाँडै सन्चो होस् (chaandai sancho hos).

lets_meet.note: Often with a time: भोलि भेटौँ न (bholi bhetaun na), 'let's meet tomorrow'.

call_me.note: Casual, to a friend: मलाई फोन गर है (malaai fon gara hai).

your_number.note: Nepalis ask a number with कति (kati), 'how much', rather than के (ke), 'what'.

have_nice_day.note: Mostly in messages; face to face, a warm नमस्ते (namaste) is usual.

good_luck.note: Used for any good wishes: exams, journeys, festivals.

thanks_a_lot.note: Warmer still: धेरै धेरै धन्यवाद (dherai dherai dhanyabaad).

miss_you.note: To an elder, say तपाईंको (tapaainko) instead of तिम्रो (timro).
